text: Pass .order = "pre" visit parents children. pre-order handler, return ast_skip(x) install x position without descending children. mirrors Pandoc Lua filters’ traverse = 'topdown' plus return el, false. Without ast_skip(), walker still descend rewritten div’s content; skip makes “whole subtree now done” explicit.
code: # Strip ALL formatting inside callout divs, leaving the rest of the # document alone. out = doc |> ast_filter(   .order = "pre",   pandoc_div = \(d) {     if (has_class(d, "callout-note")) {       flattened = pandoc_div(         attr    = d@attr,         content = as_blocks(ast_text(d))       )       ast_skip(flattened)     } else d   } )  cat(pampa_to_qmd(out)) #> # Intro #>  #> Some **bold** prose with a [link](https://example.com). #>  #> ::: {.callout-note} #>  #> Watch out #>  #> A callout with its own emphasised heading. #>  #> ::: #>  #> ## Conclusion #>  #> Final words.

title: Selecting and rewriting AST nodes
text: Two special handler names dispatch entire inline/block sequences contents rewritten: pandoc_inlines = \(xs) ... runs per pandoc_inlines wrapper. pandoc_blocks = \(xs) ... equivalent pandoc_blocks. essential context-aware transforms single-element handlers express (merging adjacent runs, dropping siblings based neighbours, etc.). List-level element-level handlers compose single pass:
code: # Drop any paragraph whose plain-text form contains "Final". out = doc |> ast_filter(pandoc_blocks = \(xs) {   keep = !purrr::map_lgl(xs@content, \(b) {     S7::S7_inherits(b, pandoc_paragraph) &&       grepl("Final", ast_text(b), fixed = TRUE)   })   pandoc_blocks(xs@content[keep]) })  select_children(out, is(pandoc_paragraph)) |>   purrr::map_chr(ast_text) #> [1] "Some bold prose with a link." out = doc |> ast_filter(   pandoc_strong  = \(el) pandoc_small_caps(content = el@content),   pandoc_inlines = \(xs) {     # Append a marker whenever a paragraph ends up containing small caps.     has_smallcaps = any(purrr::map_lgl(xs@content, S7::S7_inherits, pandoc_small_caps))     if (has_smallcaps) {       pandoc_inlines(c(xs@content, list(pandoc_str(text = "[!]"))))     } else xs   } )  # the marker landed in the paragraph that had bold: purrr::map_chr(select_children(out, is(pandoc_paragraph)), ast_text) #> [1] "Some bold prose with a link.[!]" "Final words."

title: Apply a table of type-keyed handlers to a pandoc AST — ast_filter
text: Borrows Pandoc Lua filter idiom dispatching element type: user provides one named function per S7 class rewrite, ast_filter() walks AST , invoking matching handler node. Handlers honour return-value contract map_nodes() (return node replace, list nodes splice, NULL delete, input -op). Dispatch S7 class inheritance: pandoc_block = \(b) ... handler run every block subtype. several handler names match node, first listed ... wins, put specific classes (e.g. pandoc_header) general ones (pandoc_block). Traversal post-order default: parent's handler sees children rewritten. matches Pandoc Lua filters' default. Pass .order = "pre" top-walk parent's handler runs first; pre-order handler, return ast_skip() use (possibly modified) node -without descending children. mirrors Lua filters' traverse = 'topdown' plus return el, false. Two special handler names trigger list-level dispatch entire inline/block sequences (Lua's Inlines / Blocks filters): pandoc_inlines = \(xs) ... called per pandoc_inlines wrapper contents rewritten. Return pandoc_inlines (list inlines, NULL empty). pandoc_blocks = \(xs) ... equivalent pandoc_blocks. useful sliding-window / context-aware transforms expressed single-element level (e.g. merging adjacent runs, dropping siblings based neighbours).

text: Recursively concatenates textual content pandoc AST, dropping formatting. output pampa_parse_pd() result fed back ast_text() roughly readers see document rendered flat string. Equivalent spirit pandoc.utils.stringify() Pandoc Lua filters: handy matching document content (titles, captions, link labels) without descending AST manually. Leaf rules: pandoc_str, pandoc_code, pandoc_math, pandoc_raw_inline, pandoc_raw_block, pandoc_code_block emit @text slot. pandoc_space pandoc_soft_break emit single space. pandoc_line_break emits newline. pandoc_horizontal_rule emits newline. Container rules: Block containers (pandoc, pandoc_div, pandoc_block_quote, list types, etc.) join children two newlines. Inline containers (pandoc_emph, pandoc_strong, pandoc_link, etc.) concatenate children without separator. pandoc_note emits block content (joined newlines) wrapped [^...] flag ; rarely useful match logic.
